Chapter 8: Sustaining Trust Over Time—Habits, Systems, and Renewal.
Building trust isn’t something you do just once and forget about. It’s more like tending a garden—if you ignore it, little weeds of doubt and misunderstanding can start to pop up everywhere.
So, how do you keep trust healthy as time goes on? It comes down to building habits and creating systems that help trust stay strong, even when things around you are constantly changing.
Let’s talk about a few ways to do this.
First, regular check-ins are a game changer. They give everyone a chance to clarify expectations and talk through any concerns before they become bigger problems.
Ongoing feedback—both the good and the not-so-good—keeps everyone in the loop and helps people grow.
Don’t forget to celebrate wins, big or small, and recognize the people who make a difference. That acknowledgment goes a long way.
And every so often, it’s worth revisiting your shared values and purpose. It’s easy to drift off course over time, but these conversations keep everyone moving in the same direction.
Now, let’s look at how systems can help make trust part of your culture. When everyone can see how decisions are made—when the process is transparent—there’s less room for confusion or suspicion.
Clear communication channels stop rumors from spreading, and recognition programs shine a spotlight on trust-building behavior, reminding everyone how important it is.
But even the best systems need a little renewal from time to time. Trust can fade if you start taking it for granted. That’s why it’s so valuable to pause every now and then, reflect on what’s working, and talk about what needs attention.
Sometimes this means heading out for a team retreat, having honest one-on-one conversations, or gathering anonymous feedback through surveys.
Here’s a metaphor that might help: think of trust like a bank account. You make steady deposits—positive actions, honest conversations, moments of appreciation—to keep your balance healthy.
Sure, sometimes you’ll make withdrawals. Maybe you miss a commitment or there’s a misunderstanding. But as long as you keep making those regular deposits, your trust account stays in the black.
So, what does sustaining trust look like in real life?
It means being proactive about communication, especially when things are changing.
It means tackling issues quickly, before they have a chance to grow.
It’s about showing genuine appreciation for effort, not just the final result.
And maybe most of all, it’s about staying curious and open to feedback—because that’s how you keep learning and growing together.
These habits build resilience. When tough times hit, teams and relationships with a deep well of trust can weather the storm—and often come out even stronger on the other side.
